newsitem.title: USA: Alcan targeted $300 mln annual profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Alcan targeted $300 mln annual profit rise.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd has targeted a three year increase in net income of $300 million per year, chief executive Jacques Bougie said Friday.
He said this profit target is based on 1996 metal prices without major capital investment, telling a news conference any increase in metal prices should result in a better gain.
Last month, the company reported net income of $410 million, or $1.74 per share, for 1996.
Bougie said this "would allow us to earn our cost of capital," noting Alcan has only done this twice in the past 14 years.
The overall aluminum industry has earned its cost of capital only once in those 14 years, he noted.
"Raw material costs are our disadvantage, Bougie said, noting Alcan's are "higher than (the industry) average."
The company is seeking to reduce its raw material costs to the average or lower, he said.
Stating Alcan is a buyer of bauxite, he said it is developing the Ely project in Queensland, Australia, to displace the higher cost bauxite it is purchasing on the open market.
It now expects to make a final decision on Ely in late 1997 or early 1998, he said, noting the project is now expected to cost $125 to $150 million.
Following completion of the Ely project, Bougie said, Alcan would no longer be a net buyer of Bauxite.
However, he does not expect Alcan's opening of a bauxite mine to necessarily result in a closing elsewhere, noting this capacity could well be taken up by rising demand for aluminum.
He said the company is discussing taking a minority interest in a greenfield alumina project that would start construction in four or five years.
Alcan is also nine to twelve months away from a decision on whether to proceed with a 350,000 tonne per year smelter in Quebec that would replace a 75,000 tonne plant, Bougie said.
It is also discussing a 240,000 tonne per year plant with a possible partner in China, he said.
